Prevention: Undertake deep summer ploughing to expose soil along with the pathogen to sunlight in order to reduce disease inoculum before puddling.
Use clean and healthy seeds to minimize disease occurrence.
Use 2% salt water to separate light weight and infected seeds during soaking.
Seed treatment before sowing and transplanting (see direct controls).
Apply recommended dose of urea, DAP and
MOP as per soil health crd report; avoid excessive use of urea.
Monitoring: Visit the field at weekly intervals in nurseries and after transplanting.
Be especially vigilant during periods of high temperature and high humidity as this favours disease development.
Infected plants are abnormally tall with pale, thin leaves, and produce fewer tillers.
Look for white growth of the pathogen at the base or on the lower sheath of the infected plant.
Look for adventitious roots growing from above-ground nodes on the stem.
Look for unhealthy seedlings drying from the bottom to top at early tillering stage which eventually die after few days.
Direct Control: Rogue out and destroy (burn or bury) infected or dead plants both from nursery and field as soon as identified.
